title: A Choir for the Portrait
premise: Rosalind Eastwick, a hospice nurse at Blackmere House, has always heard the dying count backwards from ten—and always in unison, as if guided by something patient. When the mirrors begin lagging one second behind reality, he learns the house's founders bound a chorus of the dead into its walls to sustain their own stolen longevity, and the ritual sustaining them is failing. Rosalind discovers his own family helped build the choir, and that the founders' descendants—including the house's charming administrator, Vivian Ashe—intend to add fresh voices before the solstice. To stop them, Rosalind must complete the counter-ritual the founders abandoned: releasing every soul they took, even though doing so will erase the last living memories of his mother, who sings among them. In the end he chooses truth over loyalty, silences the choir by singing the release alone, and walks out of Blackmere as the mirrors finally catch up—showing only himself.
about_author: Isandro Whitlock is the pen name of a former night-shift caregiver who spent six years in palliative wards across New England before turning to writing. His fiction draws on the hush of those hours, where grief and superstition share the same dim hallway.

chapters.title: The Counting Hour
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. On his night shift at Blackmere House, Rosalind hears Mrs. Halloran count backwards from ten in a voice not her own, joining a chorus of other dying patients. He keeps his rituals: lights on, doors counted. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Ten Seconds Behind
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The bathroom mirror reflects him raising a cup a full second after he does. He tests it with a dropped pen; the reflection lags again. Emotional beat: quiet vertigo—the first crack in his careful invisibility.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Administrator Vivian Ashe welcomes new staff warmly but repeats odd rules: no mirrors after midnight, never hum in the east wing. Rosalind notices she never blinks during the tour. Emotional beat: charm with teeth beneath it.

chapters.title: What Mrs. Halloran Knew
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Before dying, Mrs. Halloran grips his wrist and says, 'Don't let them finish the verse.' Her deathbed monitor flatlines in perfect rhythm with a distant hum. Emotional beat: grief braided with warning.

chapters.title: The East Wing Hymn
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Unable to sleep, Rosalind follows a faint harmony to the sealed east wing and finds a chapel of forty empty chairs facing a portrait of the founders. The humming stops when he enters. Emotional beat: trespasser's awe.

chapters.title: Vivian's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Vivian covers for his rule-breaking, offering him a permanent post and unsettling intimacy: 'You have an ear for it, like your mother did.' Rosalind realizes she knows his history. Emotional beat: flattered, then hunted.

chapters.title: Ledger of Voices
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. In the archive he finds founders' ledgers listing names beside musical notation—each entry dated on a death. The final page is blank except for a fresh ink smudge. Emotional beat: scholarly horror becoming personal.

chapters.title: His Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. One ledger signature is his mother's—dated the year she 'moved away.' He remembers no funeral, only a departure. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of his memory.

chapters.title: Reflections Out of Order
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. All mirrors in the house now lag, and some show rooms he isn't standing in—a corridor of chairs, occupied. He counts doors; there is one too many. Emotional beat: reality losing its arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Descendants' Dinner
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Vivian hosts a dinner for the founders' descendants, all unnervingly youthful for their ages. They toast 'the coming voice.' Rosalind serves wine and listens. Emotional beat: prey among predators, playing servant.

chapters.title: Forty Chairs
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He counts the chapel chairs: thirty-nine occupied by warmth he can't see, one waiting. That night, a patient dies counting, and the chair feels briefly full. Emotional beat: the ritual is nearly fed.

chapters.title: An Old Nurse's Notes
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A retired nurse mails him a box after hearing where he works: clippings about Blackmere disappearances dating back a century, all hospice staff who 'heard too well.' Emotional beat: he was recruited, not hired.

chapters.title: The Verse
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Piecing together ledger notation, he reconstructs the founders' binding hymn—it requires a living conductor each generation. The blank ledger line awaits a name. Emotional beat: understanding the trap's shape.

chapters.title: Doors Counted Wrong
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The house rearranges overnight; his counted doors now number thirteen. Trapped in a looping corridor, he escapes only by humming—ashamed how easily the house answers song. Emotional beat: the house is testing his voice.

chapters.title: Vivian's Confession, Partly
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Vivian admits the family sustains itself on the choir but frames it as mercy: 'We gave them somewhere to sing forever.' She offers him his mother's room as enticement. Emotional beat: seduction of complicity.

chapters.title: Room 12
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He opens his mother's preserved room and finds her nurse's uniform, her half-finished letter warning against 'the second verse,' which releases nothing—it harvests. Emotional beat: love and betrayal in one breath.

chapters.title: First Voice Taken
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Young orderly Marcus vanishes; his chair in the chapel is warm, and the mirror shows him seated, mouth open in silent song. Staff are told he quit. Emotional beat: guilt—he warned no one in time.

chapters.title: Ally in the Glass
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The lagging mirror begins showing him useful things: Vivian hiding keys, a door behind the portrait. Something in the glass is helping—or luring. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance with the uncanny.

chapters.title: The Founder's Journal
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Hidden behind the portrait, founder Aldous Blackmere's journal confesses the first choir was an accident: grieving singers whose deaths were caught mid-hymn. The immortality was theft they rationalized. Emotional beat: pity curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: They Know
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Vivian confronts him gently, revealing she's watched him since childhood—his mother begged for his exemption. The descendants vote to make him conductor instead of victim. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Vivian promises his mother's release if he conducts the second verse at solstice—three days away. He sees his mother's face in the mirror, nodding. Is it her or bait? Emotional beat: temptation wearing a beloved face.

chapters.title: Counting Backwards
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He begins hearing the count everywhere—in plumbing, in his own pulse. Ten. Nine. The house is counting down to solstice through him. Emotional beat: body turned instrument.

chapters.title: What the Choir Wants
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. In a lucid dream, the choir speaks through Marcus: they don't want freedom—they want to finish the hymn they died singing. Release would feel, to them, like dying twice. Emotional beat: compassion complicating rescue.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He cuts the chapel's power and salts the threshold; the house retaliates by erasing small memories—his street address, a colleague's name. Memory is the choir's currency. Emotional beat: paying for defiance in self.

chapters.title: Vivian Unmasked
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He finds Vivian's true age in the ledger—she is the founder's daughter, kept alive across four generations of borrowed voices. Her kindness was maintenance, not malice. Or both. Emotional beat: horror of long patience.

chapters.title: The Second Verse Found
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. His mother's letter, completed by pages hidden in her room, contains the counter-ritual: the release verse must be sung solo, by blood, naming every taken soul. Forgetting is the price. Emotional beat: a map drawn in sacrifice.

chapters.title: One Day Left
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He rehearses names from the ledgers while the house strips more memories—his nursing training, his reason for being here. He writes everything down like a man going under anesthesia. Emotional beat: racing erosion.

chapters.title: Marcus in the Glass
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Marcus appears in the mirror, briefly himself, begging: 'Don't finish it either way. Some cages feel like home.' Rosalind refuses to believe captivity can be kind. Emotional beat: doubt sharpening conviction.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The descendants gather in the chapel; the fortieth chair is draped in white—for him. Vivian hands him the conductor's baton, a length of blackened bone. Emotional beat: the stage set, the trap sprung.

chapters.title: The First Note
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Forced to begin the second verse, he feels the choir surge toward him, hungry and grateful at once. Mid-note, he changes key into his mother's unfinished melody. Emotional beat: rebellion inside obedience.

chapters.title: Chaos in the Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The hijacked hymn tears the house open—mirrors shatter outward, corridors unfold, the descendants age decades in seconds as their sustenance destabilizes. Emotional beat: cathartic destruction.

chapters.title: Vivian's Last Season
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Dying rapidly, Vivian stops fighting and asks only to hear the verse finished properly—she was a child when it started, she claims. He neither forgives nor refuses. Emotional beat: pity for the monster's origin.

chapters.title: Naming the Dead
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He sings the release verse, reading names from the ledgers as each chair empties. With every name, a memory burns away—his mother's laugh goes first. Emotional beat: grief as payment, willingly made.

chapters.title: Her Voice, Last
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Only his mother remains. She sings her own name so he won't have to speak it, then the chapel falls silent for the first time in a century. He cannot remember her face—but wrote a description beforehand. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Dawn. The house is ordinary, aging, mortal. Surviving staff remember nothing; the descendants are old or gone. Rosalind reads his own handwritten note: 'You chose this. Don't undo it.' Emotional beat: hollow, deliberate peace.

chapters.title: The Mirror Catches Up
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The last intact mirror shows him in perfect real time—only himself, no lag, no extra rooms. He checks the doors: twelve again. Emotional beat: reality restored, loneliness included.

chapters.title: What He Kept
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Sorting his mother's effects, he finds one thing the ritual couldn't take because it lived outside him: her letter's opening line, 'If you're reading this, be brave and be exact.' Emotional beat: inheritance beyond memory.

chapters.title: A New Post
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He takes a job at a plain, mirrorless hospice across town. On his first night, a dying man murmurs—not counting, just a name, once, humanly. Emotional beat: cautious return to the work he loves.

chapters.title: The Hum, Far Off
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Years later, he receives a letter about another house with singing walls. He packs the ledgers, his mother's line copied onto the first page, and drives toward it. Emotional beat: vigilance as vocation.

chapters.title: A Choir for the Portrait
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. In the new house's chapel hangs another founder's portrait, and beneath it, forty chairs—one already warm. Rosalind sets the ledgers on the stand and begins, quietly, to learn the names. Emotional beat: resolve without triumph; the song continues, and so does he.
